steps.content: ...The... ...sun... ...deformed...
...Demise... ...befell...

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The Apostle of Ashes is invading from the northwest of the city and is now rapidly advancing within 20 kilometers from the Broken Frontline. All combat units are to assemble to intercept the enemy. It must not enter DisSea.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Its flames contain high-intensity Mania. Beware of contamination!

FAC troops are at the forefront. Rows of anti-Mania shields collide with the flames, yet the shields of blue light shatter as the underlying equipment melts. The enemy breaks through yet another line of defense.
Like a fiery bird, the Apostle flaps its wings and Mania flames envelop everyone in scorching heat, burning your skin. Prolonged combat under high temperature nearly dehydrates everyone.

steps.speaker: FAC Officer
steps.content: Where are Paradeisos' reinforcements? Out having a picnic?! That monster is about to enter DisCity. No amount of Hypercubes can save us then!

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: ...It's not time yet. There's a more cost-effective solution.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: For the time being, hold the frontline. Paradeisos will give you the right instructions.

steps.speaker: FAC Officer
steps.content: Tsk... Squad three, retreat and regroup. Squad four, take over and hold out for as long as you can!

steps.speaker: FAC Officer
steps.content: Where are squads five and six?! Hurry up and get moving! Quick... Mmph!
With a loud thud, the sturdy wall of soldiers is breached. The soldier in front of you is blown away by the heat wave, crashing heavily to the ground and going silent.
You step forward to help up the soldier, who's still alive. The next second, a Mania storm engulfs you. You instinctively shield him with your body.
Furious shrieks pierce your eardrums. Flames consume your sanity. Clearly, you see a twisted eye of the beast drawing closer, like a gaping maw ready to swallow everyone whole.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Back off!
Red light pierces through the flames. A sharp wail bursts out as the Mania illusion is split apart. Suddenly, you see that evil giant bird impaled by shackles, struggling fiercely. You've caught it!
But the next second, it screams and the golden runes on its body suddenly ignite, forming strange patterns. The flames trace the thorns and follow the shackles, setting your entire body on fire!

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...An unseen human sorcery?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: No! The Mania is corroding the shackles! Chief, it'll hurt you, let go!

Too late. The flames are burning all over your body, using the shackles as fuel and forcing a connection between you and the Apostle. You try to retreat from the battle, but your convulsing right hand is completely out of control.

The screams and fights blur in your ears. Steam from blood and sweat distorts your vision. In the searing daze, the Apostle in front of you disappears. The adjutant and your comrades are gone, leaving only...
The sun deformed, demise befell...
Before you get a response, breathing becomes difficult. The high temperature inside you is devouring your organs. The world grows brighter, hotter.
Hills burned and charred, lives ebbed and fell.
This time, you see it as clearly as you hear it. A burning humanoid figure is drawing near.
And behind her, ten suns hang in the sky. Searing heat, blazing flames, and various mirages of Wraith Beasts are destroying an unknown city.

A force different from the Hypercubes seeps in, accompanied by weird chanting. Patterned green light spreads, suppressing the black flames and binding the fiery bird. Both the high heat and illusions are gradually subdued.
And at the end of the light patterns, on the edge of the battlefield, several unfamiliar figures appear on the burning horizon.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: ...Reinforcements have arrived. It's time.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Gather your forces, defeat the Apostle, and protect the MBCC's Chief.
